label: original-phase input of x/u/n/1/h/q/f/v at position >= 3
explanation: Almost entirely an encoding-phase unit: 99.5% of activation mass is on original-token steps, and it never fires at t=0 or 1. It is weak at t=2 and its rate rises with position (orig_idx 8 has about 5x lift). Within that window it is token-selective. x is strongest (rate 0.22, and the top examples are nearly all x), followed by u, n, 1, h, then q, f, v, with weaker graded responses to i, s, p, d. It fires mostly on the first occurrence of a token (89% of mass). It is somewhat stronger when the sequence starts with t, c, j or k. It is nearly silent at the delimiter and during copy (0.1% of copy steps). The token-and-position predicate gives dev F1 0.59 and mass recall 0.80. Many predicted steps stay inactive, especially when tokens from the same set already appeared earlier or opened the sequence, so the context dependence is graded and not captured by a simple rule. Adding in_first or n_seen conditions did not raise F1.
